name: Montbello Townhomes (Phase 1)
headline: Delwest Development Corporation plans 39 four-bedroom rental townhomes for low-income families at 14400 Andrews Drive in Denver's Montbello neighborhood, with an on-site infant-toddler daycare; the project won $1.8 million a year in federal 9% credit plus $500,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2026 Round One.
why_it_matters: It is one of very few all-four-bedroom tax credit rental projects in Denver, and it shows a stalled 4% bond deal (which lost its QCT basis boost) being reworked as a smaller 9% deal with deeper affordability and layered Prop 123, HOST and foundation money.

status.label: Credits awarded; financing closing and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award as of 2026-09-30, and OEDIT preliminarily approved $1.45M in Prop 123 Concessionary Debt in July 2026. The applicant said in early 2026 that site development plan approval and building permits were still pending and that financing would close about November 2026; There is no public closing, permit or groundbreaking record.

next_step: Watch Denver Community Planning and Development for the site development plan and building permits at 14400 Andrews Drive, and Denver City Council for a HOST loan agreement with Delwest, both of which should precede a late-2026 closing.

key_numbers.meaning: Family housing for large and multigenerational households; 8 units are built for mobility limits (2 ADA, 6 Type C visitable).
About $18M over the 10-year credit period, plus a $500,000 standard state credit award.
The applicant says incomes average 47% AMI and include 30% AMI units; OEDIT describes the range as 30% to 60% AMI. The unit-by-unit income split is not public.
State Concessionary Debt preliminarily approved in July 2026; final terms are set in underwriting.

background.text: Land history, per the applicant: a homebuilder bought the site in May 2015 and borrowed from Impact Development Fund (IDF) in 2018; after the builder defaulted, IDF foreclosed in March 2021 and held the land until Delwest bought it in July 2022 with an IDF land acquisition loan, which IDF still holds. The purchase price is not given.

The project first applied in CHFA's 2025 Round Two as a 60-unit federal 4% bond deal (requesting $1,740,450 a year in 4% credit, $19.5M in CHFA private activity bonds and $1,498,000 in state credit). It does not appear on the 2025 Round Two award report or on CHFA's rolling 4% award report.

Per the applicant, a dispute over relocating an Xcel Energy easement took up most of 2023-2024: Xcel would not vacate the easement until a new plat was recorded, and Denver would not record the plat until the easement was vacated. The delay meant the site lost its QCT 30% basis boost at the end of 2025, so the 4% structure no longer worked and Delwest switched to a smaller 9% application.

The plan changed several times after community meetings, per the applicant: in April 2023 it was 30 for-sale homes at 80% AMI and 30 rentals at 80-120% AMI; after June 2024 feedback it became a 60% AMI average 4% rental; 30% AMI units were added after a January 2025 meeting with the District 8 council member; the 2026 Phase 1 version averages 47% AMI.

Local approvals, per the applicant: Denver City Council approved the plat in summer 2025; the site development plan and building permits were still to come (about 6 months at the earliest to start work). No public source shows the council ordinance number.
Being called Phase 1 implies a later phase on the remaining land (inferred from the name; the 2026 narrative does not describe a Phase 2).
The 2025 version of the project estimated about $640,000 per townhome ($160,000 per bedroom), based on a Palmeiro Group estimate from 90% drawings; no cost figure is public for the 39-unit Phase 1.
Hoodline's May 2026 summary of the award also describes four-bedroom townhomes with an early childhood education space, all-electric design and 30-60% AMI targeting.

discrepancies.text: Hoodline puts CHFA's 2026 Round One totals at $23,003,741 in federal 9% credit and $7,000,000 in state credit, while CHFA's award report (as of 2026-09-30) totals $23,509,805 federal 9% and $6,000,000 state across the same 14 deals and 634 units.
